 Judgment

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 09.06.2014 passed in MVC No.3279/2012 by the learned XXII Additional Small Cause Judge, Court of Small Causes, and MACT, Bengaluru, whereby the claim petition came to be partly allowed awarding a sum of Rs.11,000/- as compensation fastening liability on the owner of the offending vehicle and dismissing the petition against Insurance company, the appellant-petitioner has approached this Court in appeal.

entities.text: Additional Small Cause Judge, Court of Small Causes, and MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. The brief facts are as below:
That on 12.06.2011 at about 11.30 a.m. when the petitioner was walking on the side of the road near S.S. Ghati Village, Doddaballapur taluk, the driver of the Mini Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-A-5346, proceeding from Doddaballapur side drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Consequently, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Doddaballapur, wherein first aid was given and then shifted to Chirayu hospital, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and was discharged with the advice of doctors for regular follow-up treatment.

Prior to the accident, petitioner was working as a Coolie and was earning Rs.250/- per day and due to the accident and injuries sustained by him, now he cannot do any work and suffered loss of earning.
Therefore, filed claim petition claiming compensation.

4. On issuance of notice by the Tribunal, respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel before the Tribunal and the respondent No.2 resisted the petition filed by the petitioner by filing the written statement.
Inspite of service of the notice, respondent No. 1 has remained absent and hence placed exparte.

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent in its written statement denied all the averments and allegations made in the claim petition and contended that, the petitioner is neither resident of Bangalore nor working in Bangalore and hence, the case is not falling within the jurisdiction of the Tribunal.

It has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of the Mini bus bearing Reg.No. KA-13-A- 5346 and contended that, the whole facts and situation concerning the alleged accident are manipulation and for the convenience of the petitioner to get the compensation.

Further, it has contended that, the driver of the Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-A-5346, Sri Munikrishna had no effective driving licence or badge from the concerned authority and as per the DL particulars the validity of the driving licence was only for a period from 13.12.2007 to 12.20.2010, but, as on the date of the accident, the driver had no driving licence or renewed the said driving licence.

It is contended that,
the accident was due to the fault of the petitioner and not due to the fault of the insured bus and denies the age, occupation and the treatment expenses and prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues for its consideration.
Before the Tribunal, petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P6.

On behalf of respondents, three witnesses were examined as RWs 1 to 3 and eight documents were marked as Exs.R1 to R8.
7.

On hearing both the sides, the Tribunal has allowed the petition in part, awarded a sum of Rs.11,000/- and dismissed the petition against respondent-2 Insurance Company and directed the 1st respondent to deposit the said compensation amount.
8. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court seeking enhancement.

9. The appellant contends that he had sustained traumatic comminuted inter-trochanteric fracture of femur of the left leg, lacerated wound on the head and abrasions, for which, he took treatment as inpatient for 5 days at Chirayu hospital.
It is contended that he was earning Rs.8,000/- per month and had spent Rs.25,000/- towards the incidental expenses during treatment and therefore, the compensation awarded is low.

Further, he contended that the Tribunal failed to note that the driver of the vehicle had the valid driving licence to drive LMV and the police had not chargesheeted him for non-possessing valid driving licence.
Therefore, it is contended that the fastening of the liability on the owner and absolving the insurance company is also not proper.
10. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 appeared in pursuance to the notice issued by this Court and Tribunal records have been secured.

11. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant/petitioner and the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company/respondent No.2 and perused the Tribunal records.
12.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant contended that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are reflected in the certificate issued by Chirayu hospital at Ex.P6.

Though the petitioner had not produced any other documents regarding his age, income occupation and the details of the treatment, the award of compensation of a sum of Rs.11,000/- by the Tribunal is not correct since Sri Sir Shiva Shankar V A vs Mr.Muni Krishna on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147431088/
3 the fracture of the femur itself calls for the compensation under the head of pain and suffering, food and nourishment, loss of income during laid up period and notional medical expenses.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Secondly, he contends that the fastening of the liability on the owner instead of the insurance company was illegal since the mini bus comes within the definition of the LMV, for which, the driving licence of special type of vehicle i.e. transport vehicle is not required.

13. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent Insurance Company contends that the driver was not having licence for transport vehicle and therefore, the Tribunal was right in holding that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
He submits that decision in Mukund Dewangan's case is not applicable to the case on hand.
14. The fact that there was an accident involving the mini bus bearing No.KA.13.A.5346 and that the said vehicle was driven by its driver Munikrishna is not in dispute.
Further, the fact that the said mini bus was insured with the respondent No.2 insurance company is also not in dispute.
The points that are urged are about the validity of the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle and the quantum.

15. The insurance company has produced the extract of the driving licence at Ex.R5 and it discloses that the driver had the driving licence to drive LMV- non transport vehicles from 13-12-2007 to 20-8-2021; to drive transport vehicles from 13-12-2007 to 12-2-2010.
The class of vehicles for which the driving licence was issued was for LMV and maxi cab.
Badge No.6780/92 was issued for the maxi cab.
Now the question is, whether the mini bus comes within the meaning of LMV or not?

16. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant has placed reliance on the decision in the case of Shivanna and others Vs. Bharath M.M. and others1 wherein, a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court held that, the insurance company would become liable when the driver of the offending vehicle, which was a maxi cab did possess a licence for LMV by placing reliance on the decision in the case of Mukund Dewangon Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangon Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also rely on the decision in the 2021 ACJ 1923 2017 ACJ 2011 - 10 - case of Venkatesha K.N. Vs. Thipregowda and others3 wherein a Division Bench of this Court held that "a person holding licence to drive light motor vehicle is authorized to drive all vehicles of LMV class whether transport or non transport."

entities.text: Venkatesha K.N. Vs. Thipregowda and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Then he relied on the decision rendered by the Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan's case, wherein, in para 46 it was held as below:
"46. xxx xxx xxx (i) 'Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act No.54/1994.

4 (ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

entities.text: Sir Shiva Shankar V A vs Mr.Muni Krishna
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

2022 ACJ 170 - 11 - (iii) The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f), heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h) with expression 'transport vehicle'
as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.

It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)(d) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle."
17.
In that view of the matter, the finding given by the Tribunal that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation is not sustainable.
There is no material on record to show that the mini bus driven by the driver was having unladen weight of more than 7500 kgs.

Moreover, the investigating officer also did not find that there was any violation of the driving licence and as such,
the driver was not prosecuted for non-possessing a valid driving licence.

18. Coming to the assessment of the compensation, the Ex.P6 shows that the petitioner had sustained fracture of shaft of femur of left leg, lacerated wound on centre of top of head and other multiple abrasions and therefore, he - 12 - was admitted to Chirayu hospital.
In view of the injuries sustained, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and suffering and a sum of Rs.1,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.
In the absence of any other documentary evidence by the petitioner, the nature of injuries suggest that he was unable to resume his work at least for a period of two months.
Therefore, assessing his income to be Rs.4,000/- per month, a sum of Rs.8,000/- has to be awarded towards loss of income during laid up period.

19. The amount of compensation awarded under the head of pain and suffering has to be enhanced to Rs.15,000/- and under the head of medical expenses, attendant charges, conveyance and food Sri Sir Shiva Shankar V A vs Mr.Muni Krishna on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147431088/
5 and nourishment expenses to a sum of Rs.7,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the total compensation has to be enhanced from Rs.11,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
Hence, a sum of Rs.19,000/- has to be awarded as compensation in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 09.06.2014 passed in MVC No.3279/2012 by the Tribunal, is modified by setting aside the dismissal of the petition against the insurance company and enhancing the compensation of Rs.19,000/- together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

(ii) Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount including the enhanced compensation together with interest within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
- 14 - (iii) Rest of the order of the Tribunal remain unaltered.
